paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome. This is GitHub Trending Today number 61. 35 trending open-source projects on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.

MROffice publishes six browser editors you can build into your own app, from spreadsheets and PDFs to handwriting and code. You can self-host the editors for formats like CSV and Markdown. If your app needs to edit Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files, MROffice offers a hosted embed. Your server opens an editing session and the service sends the updated file back when users save.

Kernarium runs a real Linux kernel natively inside an iOS app with no hypervisor required. Instead of emulating a full machine like UTM or faking the kernel like iSH, it compiles user-mode Linux to ARM64 machine code and runs guest apps through a multi-core interpreter. It includes Vulkan support and powers the Endarium Android emulator on iPhone and iPad.

Mobile Agent Testers is a GitHub template that runs Claude Code agents on iOS simulators and Android emulators inside GitHub Actions. Each agent plays a persona with its own device, font size, language, and dark mode setting, uses your app like a brand-new user, then writes a bug report with screenshots. On the demo app with 11 planted bugs, four testers found nine of them for 87 cents in model usage.

Open Computer lets your team hand a coding task to an agent right in a Slack thread. Tag @computer with a bug report and it starts an isolated session with Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode. Teammates can follow along and steer the fix before the agent opens a pull request for review. You can run Open Computer in your own cloud or use the hosted service.

This repo from the Lean community is a verification harness for an outside Lean formalization that claims to prove the Riemann hypothesis. It mirrors the submitted proof byte-for-byte unmodified and runs it through the comparator tool against five challenge statements built on Mathlib, including the hypothesis itself and a generalized version for Dirichlet L-functions.

Recomp Launcher helps you find and run console games that developers have recompiled to run natively on PC. Pick a project from the catalog and the launcher downloads it from the developer's GitHub release. For supported games, point it at your own disc image or game folder to finish setup. You can keep multiple versions side by side, and the launcher backs up your saves before every update.

AirHand lets you control a remote desktop through a relay you host yourself. Enter the other device's six-digit code to connect. The host uses its GPU to stream the screen at up to 120 frames per second while your device draws the pointer locally so it responds as you move. If the network slows down, AirHand skips stale frames to keep the picture current.

Songe helps your local model learn from the corrections you give your coding agent. A quick pass adds preferences you've expressed to the model's instructions. When your machine is idle, a longer pass turns corrections and tool errors into practice examples and trains a small adapter on them. Songe tests the new version against your past conversations and switches only if it scores better.

NoSpeaker makes a MacBook's Force Touch trackpad speak out loud, even with the Mac muted. Type a phrase and the app breaks a macOS voice into tiny slices, picks out two frequencies from each one, and sends those tones to the motor that makes the trackpad click. The vibrating glass produces a quiet voice you can hear. You can also play the trackpad like an instrument.

Worker 755 is a browser game where an AI manager thinks you're the sub-agent it just spawned. A task lands in your terminal and you have 90 seconds to carry it out. The manager reads your report and checks the commands you actually ran. Meanwhile, Dan, the user who hired it, is watching the chat with his family photos on the line. At the end of your shift, the AI writes your performance review.

Scene CV is a 3D resume template. You walk into a desk room at a rainy night window built in Blender and rendered in the browser with Three.js. Click the computer, the printed pages, the VHS tapes, or the bookshelf to open your about, resume, work, and reading sections. There are Steam-style achievements, a record player, and a TV that plays your own tapes. It's all static files with no build step.

Fast Anything is a CLI and MCP server that profiles apps in Python, Node, or Ruby, and lets your coding agent port only the slow functions to Rust. Before enabling the Rust version, it replays up to 500 recorded calls to prove the outputs match and keeps each swap reversible. It works with Claude Code or Codex, and the author reports a 116x speed-up on a Python demo.

Skill Distill is a skill for Claude Code or Codex that asks whether an open-weight model can do the same job with the right instructions. At the end of a session, the frontier model writes a skill for a student model, then runs the student on a clean copy of the task, compares its output to the original, and fixes the skill at the first point it fails. It repeats until the student matches.

Winedroid is an experimental Android compatibility layer for macOS, Linux, and the browser, inspired by Wine, that runs APKs without booting Android at all. It's written in Rust, executes DEX code directly, reimplements Android framework behavior, and draws app interfaces with Skia. Desktop builds add a Cranelift JIT, and a WebAssembly build runs the same runtime right in your browser.

QR Snip is a browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox that scans QR codes right off your screen. Press a shortcut, drag a box around a code, or right-click an image, and it decodes it locally with a bundled JSQR library with no network calls. Before you open a link, it warns you about plain HTTP, lookalike domains, and URL shorteners, and it blocks JavaScript and data links outright.

Signet helps teams track which versions of their AI agents and skills they've approved. Each release gets its own fixed snapshot with a record of the checks it passed, who reviewed it, and which policies applied. Before loading a skill, you can verify the signature on that release and check whether it's still certified. If the team revokes it later, that decision stays in an append-only log.

Open Artifact lets any coding agent, from Claude Code to Codex or Cursor, create editable artifacts. You can comment on slide decks, UI designs, design systems, whiteboards, spreadsheets, dashboards, and docs. The agent writes a plain folder of files, and a local daemon opens them in an editor in your browser with comments flowing back to the agent session.

Void Struck fits a space exploration game into a single 299-kilobyte HTML file. A jump drive test strands you 2,500 light-years from home. You can skim a star to refuel, land on a planet you spotted from orbit, and walk its surface. Your browser generates the worlds and synthesizes the soundtrack as you play. Every jump home costs years back on Earth, and messages start catching up with you.

Sprite Stacking is an agent skill that turns four flat pixel-art views of an object — top, side, front, and back — into a fake 3D sprite you can spin. Written in Python, it keeps a voxel only where all four views agree, then slices the volume into thin layers that get rotated and lifted a pixel each to render. A browser viewer gives you a turntable, an exploded view, and a 16-direction export.

Splat Repair lets you brush unwanted details out of a 3D Gaussian splat scan. Paint over a sticker on a wall, and Fast Fill uses the surrounding wall to estimate its shape, then copies nearby splats to patch the gap in 3D. Flat surfaces are the easy case. For a repeating pattern like the tread on a shoe, you can use the clone stamp to touch it up by hand.

Claude MultiDesktop lets you keep your work and personal Claude accounts open side by side on one Mac. A bash script creates a launcher for each account, so each window has its own sign-in and chats. Both use the same local Claude Code setup, so a skill you add once is available in either window. You can also ask a running session to message one in the other account.

Antigravity Dashboard is an unofficial usage widget for Google's Antigravity app and IDE. It sits beside the model picker or in a side panel and shows tokens per second, time to first token, cache hit rate, context window use, and how much of your 5-hour and weekly quota is left with reset countdowns. Daily and weekly grids track your history locally.

Grid Lines is an agent skill for UI alignment that draws the lines first, then moves the items. It runs a small JavaScript probe in your page that measures the real edges of text, icons, and controls, draws vertical guides down the interface, and flags anything that misses its line. Your agent then fixes the padding so sidebars, toolbars, menus, and tables share a few clean edges.

Inworld's Voice Isolator separates speech from background noise in recordings and live audio. Give the offline model a noisy voice-over and it writes two WAV files: one with the clean speech and one with the sound it removed. That lets you listen to what got filtered out or mix some room sound back in. For live calls, a streaming model processes incoming audio with 20 milliseconds of look-ahead.

Context Mode for Antigravity is a local-first plugin for Google's Antigravity app that keeps huge terminal output, build logs, and big files out of your chat history. A hook blocks unbounded dumps like cat or git diff plus oversized file reads and points the agent to indexed SQLite search instead. In the author's test, a 65 KB Unity log came back as 550 bytes, a 99% cut.

StellarHub is a control center for your Windows PC with a Python engine and a plain HTML interface in a native window. It puts live hardware stats, driver updates, an uninstaller that hunts down leftovers, a disk analyzer, and a cleanup optimizer into one app. There's a catalog of over 150 apps to install, hardware and peripheral tests, and an autopilot mode that runs your maintenance routines on a schedule.

Google DeepMind's Robotics plugin lets an Antigravity agent write a controller for a robot arm, test it in MuJoCo, and run the same code on the real arm. In the project's demo, a YAMRO picks cookies off a moving conveyor and sorts them into two boxes. You can also work entirely in simulation, rearrange the objects between runs, and watch a recording to see which pickups worked.

Restaurant AI Skills gives restaurant teams 13 ways to use an AI assistant with the menus, bookings, and sales files they already have. If you're choosing a dish to feature, the menu calculator shows how much each order contributes and how that adds up across sales. When a group dinner inquiry lands, another skill helps you draft an itemized proposal with a payment breakdown and a follow-up plan.

A Better Antivirus isn't really an antivirus. It's a Windows tripwire for info stealers written in Go that plants decoy files like a passwords text file, a wallet phrase, and fake app data for apps you don't even have. When a process touches one of those baits, it freezes that process and everything it spawned, collects forensics, and can kill it or cut the network. A built-in test runs a harmless fake stealer.

Work3 lets you run Claude Code agents in parallel, each on its own Git branch with a separate working folder. If one agent is fixing login while another builds a settings page, each gets the dependencies and environment files your team setup calls for. When a branch is ready, one command can fast-forward main to the finished commits and clean up the work tree.

Exo is a native Gmail client for macOS written in Rust and inspired by Superhuman. It connects your Mac directly to Google where you can read and send mail, organize your inbox, and manage settings like filters and signatures. Setup takes an extra step: you create your own Google sign-in client and enable the Gmail, Calendar, and People APIs before connecting your account.

ML FastFrames is Apple's research project for generating 480p video one frame at a time. Its two models use just two diffusion steps per frame. Give one a prompt about a surfing corgi and the example script produces about 5 seconds of video at 16 frames per second. The repo also includes a separate Lingbot demo where you can steer the camera as the scene unfolds.

Subtle is an agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that adds animated captions to talking-head videos rendered entirely on your Mac with no uploads and no API key. It transcribes your speech with Whisper down to the word, highlights numbers and names, and picks from 35 caption styles rendered with Remotion. In the "behind you" styles, Apple Vision cuts out the speaker so a giant word can sit behind them.

UI Diff shows reviewers what changed on screen in a pull request. It finds the affected pages and takes matching desktop and mobile screenshots before and after the change. If a button gets wider, it can highlight the changed pixels and show exactly how much its padding grew. Publish the comparison once and later runs can update the same pull request comment.

Minecraft Server on Orange Cloud runs a Minecraft Java server in your own paid Cloudflare account. Players join through your domain and the server saves the world to R2 about every 5 minutes. Once everyone's been offline for 10 minutes, it saves again and goes to sleep. The next connection wakes it up and restores the world, so the first player can join again about 30 seconds later.
